source_ref: Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation, Art. 25 data protection by design
note: Identifiable raw footage uploaded with no redaction at the edge: the privacy control the design relies on is absent.

source_ref: s. 2.3 legitimate interest, s. 3 in-vehicle processing
note: In-cabin or facial imagery under legitimate interest: EDPB treats in-vehicle monitoring of identifiable people as needing a stricter basis and a documented balancing test.

source_ref: Art. 6(1)(f) with Art. 5(2) accountability; EDPB s. 2.3
note: Legitimate interest without a documented balancing test on file: the basis cannot be relied on, and the controller cannot show the assessment if asked.
Systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area, or of people in the cabin, requires a DPIA before processing starts.
CCPA/CPRA has no lawful-basis concept; a notice at or before collection is the gating duty.

source_ref: Luat 91 Art. 21 (transfer impact assessment); ND 356 dossier rules
note: A cross-border transfer impact-assessment dossier must exist and be filed with the authority within 60 days.
No Art. 6(1) basis identified (an 'unknown' basis is not a basis).

source_ref: ambiguity escalates, it never defaults to GO

The controller must be able to demonstrate consent; with no record the basis cannot be evidenced in an audit.
